headline: Fitted mechanistic models link single-cell and patient omics to regulatory dynamics
label: Mechanistic Modeling Of Omics Data
summary: Equations fitted directly to time-resolved, single-cell, and patient multi-omic data move analysis beyond descriptive summaries.
synthesis: The dominant thread is fitting explicit dynamical or structured models to omics measurements rather than relying on descriptive summaries alone. Probability flow matching learns biophysically consistent stochastic gene-regulatory dynamics from time-resolved data, and HMCVelo fits deterministic ODE velocities for hydroxymethylation per cell and gene. A glioblastoma astrocyte digital twin is calibrated to CPTAC patient proteomics to simulate EGFRvIII and PTEN perturbations. Trajectory-focused methods include a functional KL divergence estimator applied to scRNA-seq, scTrends for trend strength along pseudotime, and scTransient for wavelet-based transient events. Equation learning across multi-experiment agent-based simulations yields continuum models, while szKendall offers a structural-zero-aware dissimilarity for single-cell Hi-C subtype discovery. What is new is calibration to patient-derived data and equation discovery that generalizes across parameter space.
